# Reading Búri through the work it rules today
If the stories are true in the way that matters, they should show up in the world without being invoked. **Búri** shows up constantly.

Búri has no adventures, no conflicts, no cult. His entire myth is cosmogonic: he is the first divine being, the point at which the inanimate cosmos becomes personal. Everything that follows in Norse mythology follows from his emergence.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **4 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.
## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Búri
- **Pantheon:** Norse
- **Domain of influence:** First God of the Norse Pantheon, Progenitor of the Æsir
- **Pattern seats:** 4
- **Sectors touched:** Commerce & Governance · Energy & Natural World
- **Strongest seat:** Ancestry & Heritage Services
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 52 of 271
## The Myth at Work

**The Licking of the Rime.** In Gylfaginning, Snorri tells how the primeval cow Auðumla licked the salty stones of Niflheimr.  On the first day, hair appeared; on the second, a head; on the third, a whole man. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.

**The Line of the Æsir.** Búri → Burr → Óðinn, Vili, Vé.  That simple genealogy underwrites the legitimacy of the Æsir. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.
## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Ancestry & Heritage Services

*Genealogy, heritage research, and DNA ancestry. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *The first god, grandfather of Óðinn; the Norse family tree starts with him.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest

*Farming, grain, food production, and agtech. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

*Auðumla, the primeval cow whose licking revealed him — dairy at the dawn of the gods.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Búri performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Mining & Natural Resources

*Extraction, minerals, and subterranean wealth. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

*Licked from the salty rime-stones; the first god is a mineral find.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

### Startups & Venture Creation

*Startups, incubators, and venture capital. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *The first god emerging from the empty rime; every founding begins from nothing.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

Read the myth again after the seats and it stops sounding ancient: Búri has no adventures, no conflicts, no cult. The age changed. The work did not.
## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity's documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. The full derivation, the weights, and the challenge process are public on the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). If a seat in this file reads wrong, the atlas itself tells you how to prove it — and the correction becomes part of the record.
## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in ancestry & heritage services, agriculture, food & harvest, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/buri/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit. The story is the pitch; the seats are just where it already works.
